title: Properties of Subsets of Unobserved Items Constructed by Using Blackwell's Bet
summary: Blackwells Bet (also known as the Cover Guessing Game) is an extremely clever use of a random variable to improve the probability of guessing which of two numbers is larger when you are only allowed to observe one of those numbers. This technique has hitherto been used to guess or predict outcomes with better-than-chance results. We show that this technique can also be used to construct subsets of unobserved items which have expected values below and above the expected value of the parent set.
